constraint_decided_it: The identity of the frozen extract relative to the clipped leg. S13 Sample's scope note: 'We typically regard a sample as ceasing to exist when the respective representative qualities become corrupted'; S11 Amount of Matter defines an amount 'by the total and integrity of their material content'; and CRMsci declares O29 removed sub-sample (S24 Sample Splitting -> S13 Sample) as yielding 'the resulting instance of S13 Sample that has been removed from the original sample', i.e. a distinct S13 instance, not the original re-labelled. Answer A's closing claim that 'the frozen extract can be the same S13 Sample instance as the removed leg tissue, just re-identified with a new P1/P48 identifier' is against all three; Answer B treats the extract as a distinct S13 with its own identifier, which is what the declared model supports.
better_modelling: (1) The moth stays E20 Biological Object (E20 < E19 < E18, and CRMsci declares S10 Material Substantial superclass of E18, so it is in range of O1/O3) under its original P48 has preferred identifier. Its paratype status is carried by P137 exemplifies (E1 -> E55) with the P137.1 in the taxonomic role property set to 'paratype' -- P137's own example is exactly a natural-history type specimen ('Object BM000098044 of the Clayton Herbarium (E20) exemplifies Spigelia marilandica (E55) in the taxonomic role lectotype'), and neither answer used it although the question turns on paratype status. (2) The leg clipping is ONE event, multiply instantiated as S2 Sample Taking + E80 Part Removal + E12 Production. S2 carries O1 diminished / O3 sampled from -> the moth, O4 sampled at -> E53 Place (the leg position), O5 removed -> S13 Sample (the leg tissue). E80+E12 is the concrete content of the instruction both answers quote from S1 ('multiple instantiation with adequate concepts of creating the respective items'): E80's own scope note says 'In cases where the part removed has no discernible identity prior to its removal but does have an identity subsequent to its removal, the activity should be modelled as both an instance of E80 Part Removal and E12 Production', and Issue 574 (Done) widened P112's range to E18 and added the Darwin Porite coral example (E20 diminished by E80) precisely so E80 covers natural-history sampling -- Martin Doerr, t1536: 'the class was also designed for cutting parts from archaeological objects, natural history stuff etc.' Both answers dismissed E80 on mischaracterisations of its scope note. (3) The DNA extraction is a SECOND event: an S2 Sample Taking whose O3 sampled from points at the leg-sample (S13 < S11 < S10, so it is in O3's declared range) and whose O5 removed points at a new S13 Sample bearing the freezer catalogue number as P48. Neither answer models the two-step; both collapse the extract into the single first sampling event. (4) Paratype provenance survives regardless of the identity decision, via the O3/O5 chain across both events.
reasoning: Both answers get the same correct core -- S2 Sample Taking (S1's scope note gives 'taking a tissue sample from a body' as a paradigm case), O1/O3 -> the moth as S10, O5 -> a new S13, the moth diminished not transformed (E80/E81: E81 is only for 'total decomposition ... such that the whole ceases to exist'), and the extract as a new object rather than the specimen's identity continued -- and all their domain/range applications check out. They part on the second half of the question. A concludes the frozen extract is the same S13 instance as the leg, which violates S11's 'total and integrity of their material content' identity criterion and S13's cessation clause, and is contradicted by O29's declaration that a sample derived from a sample is a new S13; A rests that claim on t1080, a 2018 draft-scope-note thread, and even there Niccolucci says 'when ideally the splitting arrives to the molecule level, further splitting must stop or the sample is lost', which cuts against A rather than for it. A additionally misstates E80's scope note, asserting it and P112/P113 'only cover the moth-side diminishment, not the sample's own persistent identity' when P113 removed (E80 -> E18) is exactly the link to the removed part and the scope note explicitly prescribes E80 + E12 Production for a part that gains identity after removal. B lands on the modelling the declared model supports, and all three of its quotations verify verbatim, but it presents issue332#current-s0011/s0012 as 'the SIG's own resolution of Issue 332' when those sentences are a posted comment by Thanasis Velios ('I think that we cannot guarantee...') that the SIG rejected in the same chunk -- 'the sig ... decided against it. DECISION: the sig opted for a subproperty of O3 sampled from ... Oxx split from' -- and the construct that resulted, O29, says the opposite emphasis: 'The new sample (i.e. the sub-sample) maintains the characteristic qualities of the original'. Issue 332's actual outcome is 'closed ... nothing left to do'. B also mischaracterises E80 ('only supports keeping a single identity when the removed part has no separate documentary role' appears nowhere in it). B is better on the modelling by a clear margin; its defect is provenance of authority, A's is the modelling itself.
